messages:
alicia: FYI incident where a long-running chat cutover caused duplicate completions after our handoff. Thinking we need a preemptive resume contract to reduce replays.
ben: Ugh. Can you paste the minimal trace? Did it happen during an ingress failover or client reconnect?
alicia: Ingress failover. Root: frontdoor A forwarded stream, B accepted resume but re-sent last chunk; model produced duplicate tokens. trace: ingress-id 0xabc, upstream attach at seq 124, resume token TTL mismatch.
caroline: Short takeaway: any resume contract must be explicit about 'last-acked token index' AND whether upstream should treat resume as speculative vs canonical. Otherwise side-effects replay.
ben: Agreed. Two axes: (1) resume as 'soft' (merge KV prefix) vs 'hard' (drop upstream state) (2) idempotency token per request. Tradeoffs: soft faster but can produce duplicates unless dedupe layer exists.
matt: Also need to consider memory/metadata: keeping per-stream resume history increases memory pressure. Maybe bound by window (N last tokens) and a cheap hash for dedupe.
alicia: What about a consensus handshake between frontdoor and upstream: A issues a resume claim with resume_id + last_seq; B replies ACCEPT|CONFLICT. If CONFLICT, fallback to full restart with checkpoint.
caroline: That requires synchronous metadata roundtrip—adds latency. Could we piggyback on existing control channel? If control plane is async, hedging might be simpler.
ben: Another option: adopt idempotent request semantics server-side: issue request_id and server dedupes by request_id. But for streaming with partial outputs that's messy — need chunk-level ids.
alicia: I'm leaning toward a hybrid: 1) cheap resume token (last_seq + short-hash) for fast path; 2) if mismatch or CONFLICT, automatic 'resume-to-checkpoint' fallback that asks client to resend from last checkpoint. Keep soft resume best-effort.
infra-bot: deploybot: rolled out ingress-resume-probe v0.3 to staging, opt-in via feature flag 'resume_fastpath'. Watch logs: /staging/ingress/resume/*
matt: We also need to define clear semantics for side-effects: if model triggers an external action mid-stream, replaying could double side-effects. Recommend requiring idempotency hooks for any stream that causes side-effects (or force full restart).
caroline: Agree. Update RFC: add a 'side_effects_allowed' flag on the resume contract; default false for safety. Also add TTL for resume tokens and rate-limit resume attempts per request_id.
ben: Nice. Also telemetry: emit metric resume_accept_rate, resume_conflict_rate, resume_fallback_latency. Helps tune window size.
alicia: Cool. Next steps: I'll draft a small follow-up RFC with handshake messages, token format, and fallback state machine. Can folks review by EOD?
ben: Yup.
caroline: On it.
matt: ack, will add notes on memory bounds.
alicia: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
